memory_update.text: FA should be promoted to Layer 2 verification as the cleanest underfollowed public candidate for education/work-history verification and credential screening.
EFX is the public reference anchor for employment/income verification data; use it to map dependencies of smaller background-screening vendors and payroll integrations.
COUR is a mid-cap skills/credential platform candidate, but later layers must prove that credentials are employer-recognized and monetized beyond generic online learning.

Pure-play labor-market analytics leaders such as Lightcast and Chmura appear private based on current evidence, leaving limited US-listed pure-play exposure; later searches should inspect HR/payroll software, staffing, and public-sector workforce analytics vendors for second-order public proxies.
Add FA as a direct underfollowed public candidate for credential, education, work-history, identity, and background verification exposure inside the education-to-employment data node.
Add COUR as a small-cap public candidate where the chokepoint angle is not generic online learning but skills graph, verified credentials, learner records, and employer/university pathway data.
Add PCTY as a second-order payroll/HCM data-pipe candidate feeding employment verification networks; treat as inference until monetization and scale are verified in filings.
Use EFX as the reference leader for employment/income verification infrastructure; not an underfollowed alpha lane but useful for benchmarking scale, regulation, data coverage, and pricing power.

Private/non-listed assets appear important in this node, especially Lightcast for labor-market analytics and National Student Clearinghouse for education records; later layers should map which public companies depend on or compete with these private utilities.

FA is a high-priority underfollowed candidate for the credential-verification node because it directly offers identity, background screening, education/work verification, credential checks, and ongoing monitoring, and absorbed Sterling Check in 2024.

DCBO is a small-cap hypothesis for skills-data and learner-record infrastructure after adding 365Talents skills intelligence and exposing learning/certification context to AI tools; needs proof of monetization and adoption.

COUR is a small-cap direct-but-debated candidate because its Skills Graph, Career Graph, Skills Verification, and micro-credential platform connect learners, skills, credentials, institutions, employers, and governments.
EFX/The Work Number should be treated as a reference anchor and potential dependency layer for employment and income verification, not as an underfollowed education pure play.

Pearson PLC / Pearson VUE may be a relevant US-listed ADR certification-gate candidate, but it was excluded due to the four-candidate limit; next pass should test professional certification exposure versus market-cap purity.

Lightcast appears highly relevant to labor-market analytics and education-workforce alignment, but current evidence indicates it is private/KKR-backed, so it is not a direct US-listed candidate; use it as a private benchmark when evaluating public substitutes.
PSO/Pearson should remain the reference leader for digital credentialing because Credly provides direct verified-skills and credential-network exposure.

FA/First Advantage is the best underfollowed mid-cap candidate found in this pass: education exposure is hidden inside background screening, credential verification, identity, ATS/HCM integrations, and hiring compliance workflows.
COUR/Coursera should be tracked not only as online learning but also as a proprietary skills-signal and microcredential data asset; verify monetization beyond enrollment.

SKIL/Skillsoft is a below-$300M speculative exception with direct skills-management language; survival depends on balance sheet, customer adoption, and whether Percipio skills data creates defensible recurring revenue.

Equifax was not included due to the four-candidate limit and large-cap status, but its Work Number and Verification of Education products make it an important large-cap adjacent verification anchor for later comparison.

The chokepoint may not be course delivery; it may be trusted verification rails and interoperable skills data connecting transcripts, badges, licenses, employment history, ATS/HCM systems, and workforce planning.

The cleanest public exposure is not usually labeled 'edtech': it sits in employment verification, background screening, skills platforms, high-stakes digital testing, and learner-credential records. Two-lane result: Equifax is the obvious reference asset for employment/income/education verification infrastructure; First Advantage is the strongest underfollowed small/mid-cap direct screening and credential-verification candidate; Coursera is a mid-cap skills/credential platform with learner-record and workforce-upskilling data; Duolingo is a large-cap digital assessment reference name through the Duolingo English Test, but less pure to workforce-training data. Layer 1B expands the public-company universe around the hypothesized bottleneck of trusted workforce/credential data. The cleanest listed exposure is not traditional edtech but employment/background verification, payroll-record data pipes, and skills-intelligence platforms. Reference lane: Equifax, because The Work Number is a scaled employment/income verification database. Underfollowed lane: First Advantage as a direct background/education/work-history verification provider; Coursera as a small-cap skills graph/credential data platform tied to universities and employers; Paylocity as a second-order payroll/HCM data source feeding verification infrastructure.
